guide.containerPrep: Clean the container with warm water (no soap) and ensure it is fully dry before starting.
guide.drainage: Add {depth} of {material} to the bottom of your container.
guide.separation: It's important that the [[drainage-layer|drainage layer]] be separate from the substrate if present. Most hobbyists opt for a fine mesh like a window screen, but you can also use a layer of [[sphagnum|sphagnum moss]].
guide.charcoal: Add {depth} of [[horticultural-charcoal|horticultural charcoal]] over the separation layer. Charcoal traps impurities and keeps the water cycle fresh. This is especially important if you are not using rain or distilled water.
guide.substrate.custom: Add {depth} of your custom mix: {recipe} — {article} {character} blend. Press down on the blend gently to flatten, but try not to over compact.
guide.substrate.standard: Add {depth} of a standard well-draining terrarium mix. Press down on the mix gently to flatten, but try not to over compact.
guide.placement: Plant the tallest or deepest-rooted plants first so that you can work around them: {names}.
guide.placement.fast: Note: {names} grow fast, so leave extra room around them.
guide.watering.thorough: make sure your substrate is thoroughly wetted
guide.watering.mist: give the terrarium a gentle misting
guide.seal.sealed: The building process can be stressful for plants. Seal the container completely and place in indirect light for 48 hours to stabilise.
guide.seal.lidded: The building process can be stressful for plants. Close the lid, but crack it open briefly each day for the first week to allow gas exchange.
guide.seal.open: No sealing needed. Monitor [[humidity]] closely during the first week.
guide.light.conflictLowMed: Conflicting light needs: some plants need direct sun, others prefer low or medium light. Place in [[bright-indirect|bright indirect light]] as a compromise — watch sun-lovers for [[etiolation]] and shade plants for bleaching.
guide.light.conflictBright: Direct and bright-indirect light requirements conflict. Place in [[bright-indirect|bright indirect light]] to not scorch sun-sensitive plants. Plants that need higher light requirements may not survive.
guide.light.mixedBright: Mixed light needs. Position in medium to bright indirect light — slightly further from the window than optimal for the bright-indirect plants to protect low-light ones.
guide.light.mixedLow: Mixed low and medium light needs. A medium-low indirect light spot works well — a few feet back from a bright window.
guide.firstTwoWeeks.enclosed: The first two weeks decide whether your terrarium takes. First 48 hours: keep it in indirect light and let it stabilise — if the glass fogs up so heavily you can't see in, crack the lid for a few hours to let it clear, and watch it doesn't overheat in any sun. A little wilting now is normal transplant shock, not a watering cue. Days 2–14: check daily for mould or walls that stay fogged solid, and resist adding water — a sealed build is still finding its balance and almost always has enough. Once condensation clears by midday on its own, you can close it up and let the cycle run.
guide.firstTwoWeeks.open: The first two weeks decide whether your terrarium takes. Keep it in bright, indirect light and let the plants settle — a little wilting at first is normal transplant shock, not a watering cue. Over the next fortnight, check daily that the substrate stays evenly moist (an open build dries far faster than a closed one) and watch new growth for signs the light or [[humidity]] needs nudging. Mist if the foliage looks dry between waterings.
compat.light.lethal: {a} needs {aLight} light and {b} needs {bLight} light — direct sunlight through glass creates a greenhouse effect and will cook shade-adapted plants — lethal.
compat.light.secondaryOnly: {a} prefers {aLight} light; {b} prefers {bLight} — they overlap only on a secondary (tolerated) light level and will need monitoring.
compat.light.oneStep: {a} prefers {aLight} light; {b} prefers {bLight} — one step apart and manageable.
compat.light.twoStepDirect: {a} needs {aLight} light; {b} needs {bLight}. Light needs are two steps apart — a risky mismatch.
compat.light.tooFar: {a} needs {aLight} light but {b} needs {bLight} — their light needs are too far apart.
compat.humidity.noOverlap: {a} needs {aMin}–{aMax}% humidity; {b} needs {bMin}–{bMax}%. No humidity overlap means that one or both plants will struggle.
compat.moisture.survival: {a} likes it {aMoist} soil but {b} prefers {bMoist} — in one shared substrate, one plant will struggle.
compat.moisture.secondaryOnly: {a} prefers {aMoist}; {b} prefers {bMoist} — they overlap only on a secondary (tolerated) moisture level.
compat.moisture.oneStep: {a} prefers {aMoist}; {b} prefers {bMoist} — one step apart and manageable with care.
compat.moisture.twoStep: {a} prefers {aMoist} soil but {b} prefers {bMoist} — one plant may struggle.
compat.temp.noOverlap: {a}: {aMin}–{aMax}°C; {b}: {bMin}–{bMax}°C. No temperature overlap means that one or both plants will struggle.
compat.ph.survival: {a} needs {aPh} substrate and {b} needs {bPh}. No pH overlap means that one or both plants will struggle.
compat.ph.oneStep: {a} prefers {aPh} substrate; {b} prefers {bPh} — one band apart. A near-neutral mix keeps both within tolerance.
compat.container.closed: {plant} needs airflow, so it is not suitable for a closed or lidded terrarium.
compat.container.open: {plant} prefers humid conditions — may struggle in an open container.
compat.crowding.error: {count} plants share only {area} cm² of floor.  They'll compete for root space in this overcrowded environment.
compat.crowding.caution: {count} plants share {area} cm² of floor. They may compete for space, monitor for overcrowding.
compat.gasExchange: {plant} grows fast and may deplete CO₂ quickly in this micro sealed container.

care.notif.body.settle-in: Settle in {build} — check on your new build
care.settle.card.enclosed: Your new build is in its first two weeks — the make-or-break window. Keep it in indirect light, watch for heavy fog or mould, and don't add water yet; a little wilting now is just transplant shock. The full walk-through lives in this build's guide under “Your First Two Weeks.”
care.settle.card.open: Your new build is in its first two weeks — the make-or-break window. Keep it in bright, indirect light and keep the substrate evenly moist as the plants settle; a little wilting now is just transplant shock. The full walk-through lives in this build's guide under “Your First Two Weeks.”
care.guide.water.sealed: This sealed container recycles its own water — it transpires, condenses on the glass, and runs back to the substrate, so a balanced one needs water only rarely, often just every few months. Read the glass rather than watering on a timer: light fog that clears by midday is healthy; if the walls go bone-dry, add a light mist; if they stay fogged solid for 48 hours or more, vent it for a few hours first before adding anything.
care.guide.water.lidded: This lidded container holds most of its moisture, so it needs water far less often than a potted plant — occasional top-ups over weeks, not days. Add a little only when the substrate surface looks dry and condensation is low.
care.guide.water.liddedDryClause: Lean conservative on watering for the dry-tolerant plants here.
care.guide.water.wet: Keep the substrate consistently saturated and wet. Ensure there is steady water pooling slightly at the base of the drainage layer at all times.
care.guide.water.mixed: Mixed moisture needs detected. Target watering precisely toward the roots of moisture-loving plants while allowing sections housing dry-tolerant varieties to stay well-drained. Avoid uniform overwatering.
care.guide.water.moist: Keep the substrate consistently damp but not waterlogged or soggy. Water evenly whenever the top surface begins to feel slightly dry.
care.guide.water.moderateDry: Allow the top layer of the substrate to dry out noticeably between waterings. Be highly conservative with watering to safely accommodate dry-tolerant species.
care.guide.water.moderate: Allow the top half-inch of the substrate to dry out between waterings, then water moderately to re-moisten without fully saturating the lower profile.
care.guide.water.dry: Water very sparingly. Allow the substrate to dry out completely between waterings to prevent root rot.
care.guide.humidity.sealed: This sealed container naturally traps ambient moisture to maintain high humidity levels ({range}). Monitor for excessive glass condensation; if the walls remain completely fogged for over 48 hours, open the enclosure for a few hours to vent stale air, then reseal.
care.guide.humidity.lidded: This lidded container helps retain elevated humidity levels ({range}). Keep the lid closed and mist periodically only when internal air circulation or the substrate surface feels notably dry.
care.guide.humidity.open: This open container allows humidity to dissipate rapidly into the surrounding room. Since your selected plants thrive with higher humidity ({range}), mist the foliage frequently, utilize an automated mister, or position a pebble tray underneath the container to boost local humidity levels.
care.guide.light.conflict: Highly conflicting light requirements detected within this ecosystem. Place the terrarium in bright, indirect sunlight as a fragile compromise. Monitor direct-sun plants for stretching (etiolation) and low-light varieties for leaf bleaching.
care.guide.light.direct: Place in a location that receives several hours of direct sunlight daily. Monitor temperature closely, as enclosed glass containers can create a greenhouse effect and overheat rapidly under direct sun rays.
care.guide.light.brightIndirect: Position the setup in bright, indirect sunlight (such as close to an east-facing window or behind a sheer curtain on a south/west window). This provides optimal energy while safeguarding delicate leaves from scorching.
care.guide.light.medium: Place in a medium indirect light environment or a few feet back from a primary light window. Avoid deep, dark corners as well as intense, burning direct sun rays.
care.guide.light.low: Tolerates low-light baselines exceptionally well. Ideal for north-facing windows, lower-light rooms, or placements sitting deeper within a brightly lit living area.
care.guide.trimming: Mixed growth rates detected within the enclosure ({rates}). Regular pruning intervals are highly recommended: monitor fast-growing elements closely and trim them back regularly to prevent them from choking out slower companions or creating canopy shadows that block valuable light.
